summary: A batch of correctness and maintainability improvements to the App Builder V2 framework itself, headlined by removing the stale live-coordination state that PR #22 leaked onto main and guarding against its recurrence, plus targeted Windows, operator-UX, and code-structure improvements that strengthen the core loop without adding dependencies.
goals: main never carries live coordination state (claims/queue/handoffs); doctor fails loudly if it ever does again
Windows operators have a documented, reliable test command that does not depend on PowerShell execution policy
Human operators can read coordination status as a concise table without breaking the JSON contract agents depend on
cli/appbuilder.js is split into focused modules so it stays maintainable as the framework grows
Token/session budgeting is concrete guidance reusing existing fields, not a speculative new subsystem
All of the above land without adding a single runtime dependency

features.name: Coordination-state drift guard + clean main
features.description: A doctor check (coordination:tracked-state) that hard-fails when coordination/claims, coordination/queue, or coordination/handoffs are tracked on a normal branch, plus the one-time cleanup that removes the 13 stale files from main and gitignores those subtrees. Combined so main is green on merge.

features.name: Windows-friendly canonical test command
features.description: Document node --test as the canonical, cross-platform test invocation and note the PowerShell npm.ps1 execution-policy caveat, so npm test failures stop tripping up Windows operators.

features.name: Human-friendly status view
features.description: A --human flag on appbuilder status that renders a concise table (claim, branch, expiry, next action) derived from existing status data, while keeping JSON as the default output so agents are unaffected.

features.name: Modularized CLI
features.description: Behavior-preserving refactor of cli/appbuilder.js into cli/lib modules (git, coordination, plan, validate) with the entrypoint as a thin router, isolating the schema validator as the seam a future validation upgrade would build on.

features.name: Concrete token/session budget guidance
features.description: Extend .agent/rules/token-use.md with concrete budgeting guidance (task-size estimates reusing files_touched_estimate, per-session and weekly heuristics, handoff-compression rules). Guidance only, no engine, no RAG.

constraints: Zero runtime dependencies — no AJV or other libraries added (AJV is explicitly deferred to a future conscious decision)
No LLM inside the CLI; commands stay deterministic scaffolding/validation/coordination
Every code change is test-first; the existing suite is the safety net for the refactor and must pass unchanged
Do not break the status JSON output contract that agents consume
Never work on main directly; never hand-edit live coordination state — go through the CLI
Anti-bloat: no new folders/services/commands beyond what these features require
